item.title: Kov\'acs Vanishing for Excellent Log Canonical Threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.33321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a vanishing theorem of S. Kov\'acs for excellent log canonical threefolds whose closed points have perfect residue fields of sufficiently large characteristic. This vanishing theorem roughly says that LC threefold pairs are not far from being rational pairs (in the sense of Koll\'ar \& Kov\'acs and Schwede \& Takagi) if one includes a correction term. We apply this vanishing to prove a depth relation of Chou and resolution-invariance of cohomologies of ``essential divisors" for isolated log canonical threefolds in large characteristic, extending works of Ishii and Fujino. Using examples constructed by Bernasconi and Cascini-Tanaka, we show that these results fail in low characteristic. Finally, we show Kov\'acs and Alexeev-Hacon's result (in char 0) that ``Irrational centers are LC centers" fails in every positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Ajit, Shikha Bhutani

item.title: Gerbe-corrected stringy E-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define an invariant of $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein complex varieties with at worst log-terminal singularities equipped with a rational Brauer class $\alpha$ that generalizes existing versions of the $\alpha$-corrected stringy $E$-polynomial, which are defined only for quotients of quasi-projective varieties by finite groups. Using recent results from $p$-adic integration, this new invariant can be shown to behave well for degenerate dual abelian fibrations and to agree with the intersection or BPS $E$-polynomial for certain moduli problems.
item.dc:creator: Michael Groechenig, Evan Sundbo

item.title: Primitive Collections for Klyachko Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.33491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Klyachko introduced a family of $S_m\times S_n$-invariant toric Gorenstein Fano varieties, $X_{mn}$, with connections to representation theory, algebraic groups, and graph theory. He focused on the case in which $m$ and $n$ are coprime, for which $X_{mn}$ are smooth, and hence Fano. Klyachko and Voskresenskii later proved that all forms of $X_{mn}$ are stably rational when $m, n$ are coprime, and that all forms of $X_{mn}$ are rational when $n$ is congruent to 1 modulo $m$. In the same paper, they classified centrally symmetric toric Fano varieties as products of projective lines and generalized del Pezzo varieties, $X_{2,2k+1}$. For this reason, the special case of generalized del Pezzo varieties are frequently studied. For example, Ballard, Duncan, and McFadden proved that the bounded derived category of generalized del Pezzo varieties has a full exceptional collection of line bundles. An understanding of the maximal cones and primitive collections of the fan associated to $X_{2,2k+1}$ is crucial in their construction. In this paper, we focus on the Klyachko varieties $X_{mn}$ in the case in which $n$ is congruent to 1 modulo $m$. We determine a description of the maximal cones and primitive collections for the associated fan. We also determine a description of their cohomology ring and some stability results on the $S_m\times S_n$-orbits of maximal cones and primitive collections for $X_{mn}$.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Lemire, Jason Palombaro

item.title: Simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.33638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we provide a partial classification (necessary conditions) for all possible simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $A$ be such an abelian variety, i.e. $A$ is simple over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and splits as $A \sim B^s$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ for some simple abelian variety $B$. Assume that $d$ is a minimal extension degree over which $A$ splits and $B$ has a minimal field of definition (up to isogeny) $\mathbb{F}_{q^e}\subseteq \mathbb{F}_{q^d}$. For dimension $2$, Howe and Zhu showed that the only possible degrees $d$ are $2$, $3$, $4$, and $6$. Moreover, for each such degree $d$, they provided explicit formulae expressing the isogeny invariant, namely the characteristic polynomial of the Frobenius endomorphism $\chi_{A,q}$, in terms of the coeffients of $\chi_{B,q}$. We extend this result to ordinary abelian varieties of higher dimension. For dimensions $3$--$10$, we provide complete lists of such varieties as components of the Weil restriction $W_{\mathbb{F}_{q^d}/\mathbb{F}_q}(B)$ together with all possible triples $(d, e, s)$ and restrictions on characteristic polynomial $\chi_{A,q}$ of the form $\chi_{A, q} \mid \chi_{V, q}$. Here, $V$ is a component of Weil restriction $W_{\mathbb{F}_{q^d}/\mathbb{F}_q}(B)$ containing $A$ as an isogeny factor and having explicit expression of the characteristic polynomial $\chi_{V,q}$ in terms of coefficients of $\chi_{B,q^e}$. For higher dimensions, we propose an algorithm for enumeration of all possible cases for a given dimension of $A$. We also provide an implementation of this algorithm.
item.dc:creator: S. A. Novoselov

item.title: A fake quadric that is not a bidisk quotient
item.description: arXiv:2611.33669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a construction of a fake quadric $S$ that is a $32$-fold branched cover of $\mathbf{CP}^1\times\mathbf{CP}^1$ along nine curves. This configuration is given by four horizontal lines, four vertical lines and the diagonal. We show that $S$ is not aspherical. As a corollary the universal cover of $S$ is not the bidisk $\mathbf{H}\times\mathbf{H}$.
item.dc:creator: Zolt\'an Szab\'o

item.title: Semiorthogonal decompositions of limit categories for symmetric stacks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our earlier work with Tudor Padurariu, we introduced the notion of limit categories for derived stacks with self-dual cotangent complexes and used them to formulate the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture. In this paper, we generalize the notion of limit categories to a broader class of derived stacks, which we call symmetric stacks. One of the motivations for this generalization is to formulate Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type correspondences for a broader class of moduli stacks. We establish several fundamental properties of limit categories for symmetric stacks, including compact generation, the existence of semiorthogonal decompositions, functoriality, and a Kunneth formula. In a companion paper, we apply the results of this paper to formulate a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for moduli stacks of sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anticanonical divisors.
item.dc:creator: Yukinobu Toda

item.title: The Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for smooth surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.33778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a general theory of limit categories for symmetric stacks, we construct their semiorthogonal decompositions for moduli stacks of pure one-dimensional coherent sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors. The components of these semiorthogonal decompositions are quasi-BPS categories associated with the corresponding local Calabi--Yau threefolds. By comparing these semiorthogonal decompositions with those of dg-categories of coherent sheaves on moduli stacks of semistable sheaves, we propose a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for surfaces, generalizing the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture for $\GL_r$-Higgs bundles. Our conjecture includes a correspondence for Higgs bundles twisted by sufficiently ample line bundles on curves. We discuss examples and construct Hecke actions on limit categories and, under certain conditions, on quasi-BPS categories. For symplectic surfaces, these actions are expected to provide a categorical lift of the corresponding Hecke operators on BPS cohomology constructed by Davison--Hennecart--Kinjo--Schiffmann--Vasserot.
item.dc:creator: Yukinobu Toda

item.title: Decomposition algorithms for rational curves on real classical groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.33837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to an algorithmic investigation of the decomposition problem for rational curves on real classical groups. The main contributions are: (1) We present two Maple-implemented algorithms for decomposing rational curves on real classical groups. The first algorithm decomposes a curve with multiple poles into a unique product of curves with single poles. For rational curves on (indefinite) orthogonal groups, the second algorithm further decomposes single-pole curves into products of low-degree curves. The former only involves linear equations, whereas the latter requires solving both linear and quadratic equations. (2) We compare the decomposition of the same curve with respect to different ambient groups. Through this comparison, we provide an interpretation of the "multiplication trick" for motion polynomials within our framework. Moreover, we demonstrate that our second algorithm aligns with this trick. (3) We prove that the solvability of linear equations in the second algorithm is preserved under the extension of the ambient group. For illustration, we provide comprehensive computational examples.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Li, Zijia Li, Ke Ye

item.title: The Brauer--Manin obstruction to weak approximation on a constant K3 surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.33908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a constant supersingular K3 surface over every global field of characteristic two for which rational points are Zariski dense but are not dense in the Brauer--Manin set. This shows that the analogue of Skorobogatov's conjecture over global function fields does not hold for supersingular K3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Valloni

item.title: The irreducibility of tame character varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.33976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tame character varieties are known to be irreducible when the parametrised local systems have monodromies lying in closures of generic conjugacy classes; we will establish their irreducibility without the genericity assumption. A combination of nonabelian Hodge correspondence and variation of parabolic weights reduces the problem to the case of almost generic semi-simple monodromies, which is then treated using a point-counting result of Scognamiglio for nongeneric character stacks. The connectedness result is then used to clarify a couple of facts concerning the symplectic leaves.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Shu

item.title: The Exact Nef-Curve Cone Formula for dlt Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.34041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an exact rational-curve formula for the nef-curve cone of every complex projective dlt pair with effective real boundary, answering the related question proposed by Cascini. Every $(K_X+\Delta)$-negative extremal ray is generated by a movable rational curve whose normalization is free in the smooth locus. We reduce the klt case to known results and treat the remaining limiting rays with a new argument based on an orthogonal movable divisor and induction on dimension.
item.dc:creator: Jingcao Wu

item.title: The asymptotics of maximal rank of three-way tensors
item.description: arXiv:2611.34052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the maximal rank of an $n\times n\times n$ tensor is $n^2/3+O(n^{3/2})$, over the real numbers and over every algebraically closed field. More generally, in format $\lfloor an\rfloor\times\lfloor bn\rfloor\times\lfloor cn\rfloor$, with $a,b,c>0$ fixed, the leading term is $\frac{abc}{a+b+c}n^2$. The argument starts with a criterion for rank with respect to an arbitrary projective variety: a decomposition of zero with surjective differential, from a smooth parameter space, bounds the rank of every point. For Segre varieties, we construct such decompositions using a basis of units in a split algebra. We also give an optimized finite bound and a closed estimate with explicit constants for the maximal rank.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Buczy{\'n}ski, Mateusz Micha{\l}ek

item.title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.34174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We introduce two new families of equivariant symmetric functions for each of types B and D and prove that these functions represent the classes of the structure sheaves of Schubert varieties and the ideal sheaves of their boundaries, respectively. We establish several fundamental properties of these functions, including translation factorization formulas and explicit expressions for the classes indexed by small affine Grassmannian elements. In type D, we further describe the action of the affine Dynkin diagram automorphism interchanging the two spin nodes and show how it intertwines the Schubert bases with a nontrivial transformation of the equivariant parameters.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Brahma, Takeshi Ikeda, Mark Shimozono

item.title: Ramification divisors and twisted Nambu brackets of Keller maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.34216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a polynomial map $\phi\colon\A^n\to\A^n$ we study the Yau twist of the Jacobian Nambu bracket by $\phi^*$. The Hamiltonian fields of pulled back functions span the image of the adjugate of $d\phi$, so the twist detects the ramification divisor of $\phi$. For a Keller map $F$ the twist is removable exactly when $F$ is an automorphism; otherwise $F$ is not proper, and every projective extension of $F$ has a non-zero effective ramification divisor supported on the boundary, whose image is the non-properness set. These results apply to every counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture and to families of Keller maps. For the explicit three-dimensional counterexample we show that $\A^3$ is the variety of binary cubic forms of a special shape with a marked simple root, and that $F$ forgets the root. This gives the degree, the fibres, the non-properness set, the monodromy and the structure of the twisted ternary algebra. Three examples modelled on weighted scrolls illustrate equivariance, degeneration to an automorphism, and an $A_1$ singularity of the fibre.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Mboya, Stephen Mboya, Carringtone Kinyanjui

item.title: Regularity Criteria for Ind-Sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2611.34231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the Kashiwara-Schapira regularity conjecture [Conjecture 6.4, Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira, Microlocal study of ind-sheaves I: micro-support and regularity, 2003] in arbitrary dimension. For this purpose, we show that under suitable finiteness and isotropic micro-support conditions, ind-sheaves which are regular on the zero section come from $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaves. Furthermore, we characterize the essential image of constructible sheaves under the natural embedding functor, and relate them to regular holonomic $\mathcal{D}$-modules via the regular Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. Moreover, we present a non-characteristic deformation lemma and a microlocal Morse lemma for regular ind-sheaves as an application of the main theorem.
item.dc:creator: Yohei Ito, Ryosuke Sakamoto

item.title: On dual varieties of smooth projective varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.34498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a smooth irreducible nondegenerate complex projective variety $X\subsetneq\mathbb P^N$, we prove that its projective dual $X^\vee$ is a hypersurface whenever $\operatorname{dim} X\ge3\operatorname{codim}X-2$. This result may be regarded as further evidence for Hartshorne's complete intersection conjecture. We also prove the duality defect conjecture of Landman in codimension at most five. Finally, we complete Ein's classification of smooth nondegenerate complex projective varieties with smooth projective dual. The list consists of smooth quadrics, the Segre varieties $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^m$ with $m\ge2$, the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(2,5)$, and the spinor tenfold in $\mathbb P^{15}$.
item.dc:creator: Timofey Fedorov

item.title: On the Gorenstein property of local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.34580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local models are used to model, \'etale-locally, the singularities of integral models of Shimura varieties. They are defined in terms of linear algebra and admit explicit descriptions by matrix equations. We determine exactly which local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ are Gorenstein. On one hand, this gives the analogous information for integral models of Shimura varieties for unramified unitary groups with parahoric level structure, and on the other hand also results in certain natural matrix equations defining non-Gorenstein singularities.
item.dc:creator: Siyu Peng

item.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
item.description: arXiv:2611.34594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mari\~no conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces. Both of these cases present a sign issue not present in the known trivial canonical bundle cases, which we show implies that the mirror symmetry predictions cannot hold for varieties with torsion canonical bundle, even up to sign.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Ab\'anades-Joglar, Dennis Eriksson

item.title: Connectedness Principle in the Complex Analytic Setting
item.description: arXiv:2611.34654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if $(X,B)$ is a normal compact K\"ahler pair and $f:X\to Z$ is a proper morphism with connected fibers to a normal compact K\"ahler variety $Z$ such that $(-K_X+B)$ is nef over $Z$, then $\mathrm{Nklt}(X,B)\cap f^{-1}(z)$ has at most two connected components for every $z\in Z$. More generally, we prove the result for generalized pairs whose nef part is allowed to be transcendental. Moreover, we record that the same result holds for projective morphism between analytic varieties (possibly non-compact).
item.dc:creator: Swapnajit Das

item.title: Zero-cycles and holomorphic forms in families
item.description: arXiv:2611.34774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish parallel Chow and Hodge-theoretic rigidity theorems for dominant projective morphisms between smooth complex varieties. For instance, if the general fiber satisfies $CH_0(F) = \mathbb{Z}$, then the same is true of every fiber. Similarly, if the general fiber is connected with $H^0(F, \Omega_F^p) = 0$ for $p > 0$, then the same is true of every fiber. This extends the case of rationally connected fibrations from [Bur26]. We further introduce higher Chow-theoretic notions of singularities.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Burke

item.title: Quot schemes on projective space
item.description: arXiv:2611.34844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop general methods for studying Quot schemes on projective space, including a new construction of components with no common neighbours. We show that the radius of Hilbert and Quot schemes can grow linearly with the dimension of the subschemes being parametrized, and construct the first examples of Hilbert schemes of curves with radius two. For absolutely split bundles on projective space, we construct a distinguished generically smooth component and classify all smooth Quot schemes. In most cases, we give explicit geometric descriptions in terms of products of generalized flag varieties and projective bundles over Grassmannians.
item.dc:creator: Ritvik Ramkumar

item.title: Invariance of log plurigenera in families of compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.34933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(X_t,B_t)$ be a smooth proper family of pairs with K\"ahler fibres, where the boundary has relative simple normal crossings and real coefficients in $[0,1)$. We show that for every $m\ge1$, every section of $mK_{X_t}+\lfloor mB_t\rfloor$ extends locally over the base. In particular, the log plurigenera are locally constant, and for $B_t=0$ we obtain the deformation invariance of the plurigenera $P_m(X_t)$. Since the total space need not be K\"ahler, we run the minimal model program on the central fibre, using the work of Hacon-Wang and Hacon-Xie, and extend its steps over a disc. The obstruction to lifting a jet vanishes along the fixed part determined by the final model, and so it is square-integrable for the weight in the extension theorem of Cao-P\u{a}un. As an application, if the adjoint is pseudoeffective on one fibre, then the pair has a relative good minimal model near each point of the base and a relative canonical model over the whole base.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu

item.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.33572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Lookup Conjecture of Boe-Graham proposes a Bruhat graph criterion for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties in the flag variety $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}$ of a complex reductive group. Its extension to Kac-Moody groups of affine type $\widetilde{A}_n$ was considered by Graham-Li. We prove the original conjecture as well as its extension to $\widetilde{A}_n$. Our method could be applied more generally to any Kac-Moody group after checking the rank-three reflection subgroups of its Weyl group. We also prove a parabolic version of the Lookup Conjecture for the type $A$ affine Grassmannian, where a stronger Bruhat graph degree monotonicity property in fact holds, and discuss the implication via the geometric Satake correspondence for weight multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: Christian Gaetz, Yibo Gao

item.title: Singularities in global pluripotential theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.33697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This book is an expanded version of the author's lecture notes at the Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (IASM) at Zhejiang University. We systematically develop the theory of plurisubharmonic singularities on compact K\"ahler manifolds and relate it to the non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and toric pluripotential theory.
item.dc:creator: Mingchen Xia

item.title: Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings, with applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers
item.description: arXiv:2611.33994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings and give applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers. We realize rational double points of ADE over $W(k)$ as invariant subrings $A^G$, where $A$ is a ramified two-dimensional complete regular local ring and $G$ is a finite linearly reductive subgroup scheme of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,W(k)}$. We also prove a general theorem on the existence of Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings: if a flat affine group scheme $G$ over $W(k)$ admits a functorial Reynolds operator and a relative Frobenius lift, then any formal power series ring equipped with a linear action of $G$ admits a Frobenius lift that restricts to a Frobenius lift on the invariant subring. Building on these results, we construct perfectoid towers arising from rational double points in mixed characteristic. We identify their tilts with the perfect towers arising from rational double points in positive characteristic of the same ADE type.
item.dc:creator: Kazuki Hayashi

item.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
item.description: arXiv:2611.34110v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hock, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: Irreducible trinomials over the binary field: an elliptic-curve criterion and explicit families
item.description: arXiv:2611.34282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study irreducible trinomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Using an elliptic curve and reciprocity laws, we prove that, for $k \ge 2$, $X^{(4^k+2)/3}+X+1$ is irreducible if and only if $4^k+3$ is prime and $2$ is a primitive root modulo that prime. By power substitution and linearization, we also assemble explicit infinite families of irreducible trinomials $X^m+X^n+1$ in fourteen distinct reduced exponent classes.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Fu, Zhiming Li, Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on polarized manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.34342v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system $T$ on the space of Fubini--Study metrics of a polarized manifold $(X,L)$, whose fixed points are the balanced metrics. In \cite{S}, Sano proves that the iterates of $T$ converge to a balanced metric, provided that a balanced metric exists and the automorphism group of $(X,L)$ is discrete modulo scalars. We remove the assumption on the automorphism group. Moreover, we show that the convergence is exponential with the optimal rate $\rho_*$ given by the linearization of $T$ at a balanced metric, which extends a result of Ioos and Polterovich (\cite{IP}) for discrete automorphism groups. We compute $\rho_*$ for $(\CP^n,\mathcal{O}(d))$ and $(\CP^1\times\CP^1,\mathcal{O}(d,d))$; for $\CP^1$ this confirms the rate obtained numerically by Sherman (\cite{Sh}).
item.dc:creator: Reza Seyyedali

item.title: Cohomology of pseudo-reductive groups over local function fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.34570v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a pairing which describes the first Galois cohomology of a pseudo-reductive group $G$ over a local function field $K$ as the Pontryagin dual of the group $\Ext^1(G, \Gm)$ of translation-invariant line bundles on $G$. In order to accomplish this, we endow the Picard group of a scheme $X$ over a (Hausdorff) topological field with a topology, and prove that this topology enjoys favorable properties under certain mild conditions on $X$ and on the field.
item.dc:creator: Zev Rosengarten

item.title: Weitzenbeock's theorem in arbitrary characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.34749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let \(k\) be a field and \(V\) a finite-dimensional rational representation of the additive group \(\GG_{a,k}\). We show that the ring of invariants \(k[V]^{\GG_a}\) is finitely generated in every characteristic, extending Weitzenb\"ock's classical theorem beyond characteristic zero.
item.dc:creator: Dominic Bunnett

item.title: Splitting of abelian varieties in motivic stable homotopy category
item.description: arXiv:2406.05674v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we discuss the motivic stable homotopy type of abelian varieties. For an abelian variety over a perfect field $k$, a top-dimensional cell always splits off in the motivic stable homotopy category $\text{SH}(k)$. Let $k=\mathbb{R}$. If $X$ is a real abelian variety of positive dimension $g$, there is, for $\mathbb{Z}[1/(2g)!]\subset\Lambda\subset\mathbb{Q}$, a concrete splitting in $\text{SH}(\mathbb{R})_\Lambda$ determined by the Deninger--Murre decomposition of the motive of $X$ and the real points $X(\mathbb{R})$. With rational coefficients, we also discuss its refinement from the viewpoint of K\"unnemann's Lefschetz decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Liu

item.title: On the splitting of surfaces in motivic stable homotopy category
item.description: arXiv:2406.11922v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over a perfect field of characteristic zero, we study when the top cell splits off from a pointed smooth projective surface in motivic stable homotopy, with K3 surfaces as the main example. Adams--Riemann--Roch and the motivic Adams relations give a uniform top-codimension annihilator. This yields an integral extreme-cell splitting in particular for complex projective K3 surfaces. Chow--Witt correspondences also yield noncanonical three-term decompositions of Milnor--Witt motives with extreme Tate summands and a nilpotence criterion for lifting finite systems of Chow projectors. In positive characteristic, the annihilator statement holds after inverting the characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Liu

item.title: On the Hodge theory of toroidal embeddings and corresponding vanishings
item.description: arXiv:2410.09899v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove $E_1$-degeneration of the logarithmic Hodge--de Rham spectral sequence for proper toroidal triples. For a compatible Weil divisor, we realize the associated twisted logarithmic de Rham complex as the filtered de Rham complex of an object in the bounded derived category of mixed Hodge modules. We use this realization to prove a vanishing theorem of Kawamata--Viehweg type for toroidal triples. We also prove relative Bott vanishing in the toric case. On the local toric charts of a toroidal triple $(X,!B,*C)$, we characterize when the canonical exchange morphism between the two ordered extensions of the constant sheaf on $X\setminus(B+C)$ is an isomorphism, when each order recovers the logarithmic de Rham complex, and when this complex is perverse.
item.dc:creator: Chuanhao Wei

item.title: Uniform lower bound of arithmetic Hilbert--Samuel function of hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2410.12821v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we give an explicit and uniform lower bound for the arithmetic Hilbert--Samuel function of projective hypersurfaces in the framework of Arakelov geometry. The bound has optimal dependence on the height of the varieties. As an application, we use this lower bound to study the determinant method.
item.dc:creator: Chunhui Liu

item.title: Moduli of non-pure sheaves and contractions of Hilbert schemes
item.description: arXiv:2508.13395v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define certain stacks of rank one sheaves on a smooth projective variety, and show that they admit proper good moduli spaces. We offer several applications to contractions of subschemes inside Hilbert schemes of points. We construct a surgery diagram via non-GIT wall-crossing, and use the interpretation of the surgery as a fine moduli of sheaves to prove instances Kawamata's DK-hypothesis in this setting.
item.dc:creator: Andres Fernandez Herrero, Svetlana Makarova

item.title: Algebraic cycles on some Fano varieties. Part I: Quartic double fivefolds
item.description: arXiv:2509.12186v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study algebraic cycles on quartic double fivefolds, which are Fano fivefolds whose middle cohomology is numerically similar to that of a Calabi-Yau threefold, continuing the work of Skauli on lines, $1$-cycles and the coniveau filtration on double covers of projective space. By means of cubic surfaces which are totally ramified along the branch locus, we prove the integral Hodge conjecture for all of them. We also show that the comparison maps between their Chow groups and \'etale Chow groups are isomorphisms except possibly in codimension three, where we describe the kernel and the cokernel in terms of Bloch-Ogus cohomology and, via a Sarkisov link, of the unramified cohomology of a cubic surface over the function field of $\mathbb{P}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Montero, Iv\'an Rosas-Soto

item.title: On Casagrande-Druel Fano varieties with Lefschetz defect 2
item.description: arXiv:2510.20732v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The larger the Lefschetz defect delta(X) of a smooth complex Fano variety X, the more information we can deduce about the geometry of X. The structure of varieties with delta(X) greater than 2 is known. In this paper, we study the case delta(X)=2. In particular, we focus on Fano varieties with delta(X)=2 arising from the so called Casagrande-Druel construction, which we refer to as Construction A. We show that among the 19 families of Fano 3-folds with delta(X)=2 classified by Mori and Mukai, 15 arise from such construction. Moreover, we construct all Fano 4-folds with Picard number greater than 3 and delta(X)=2 admitting such a structure, obtaining 145 distinct families in total. This completes the classification of all Casagrande-Druel Fano 4-folds with delta(X)=2. To broaden the scope, we also study a generalized version of Construction A, which we call Construction B, and we show that 18 out of the 19 families of Fano 3-folds with delta(X)=2 arise from it.
item.dc:creator: Pier Roberto Pastorino

item.title: Conics and rational points of bounded height on cubic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2601.10895v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct auxiliary intersections covering points of bounded height on geometrically integral non-ruled cubic surfaces over a fixed number field, and prove uniform bounds for the contribution of their conic components to rational and integral point counts. In the affine case, when the section at infinity is geometrically integral, the conic contribution admits a bound with a height exponent strictly below one. Under these hypotheses and within the same covering, obtaining a uniform bound for all integral points with any exponent greater than one reduces to controlling components of degree at least three. The proof combines a form of the global determinant method that retains the dependence on the height of Cayley form with uniform estimates for the number of conics of bounded height. The Deligne pairing and the geometry of residual conic pencils yield cubic image curves in fixed coefficient spaces. Uniform point estimates on these curves control the distribution of conic heights, with constants independent of the surface and the pencil.
item.dc:creator: Chunhui Liu

item.title: Birational $\mathbb P^2$-bundle structures and toric 2-Fano manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.18054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a general birational program toward the classification of toric 2-Fano manifolds through the investigation of the minimal projective bundle dimension \(m(X) \in \{1,\dots,\dim(X)\}\) introduced in our previous work. This invariant captures the minimal degree of a dominating family of rational curves on \(X\) and admits a natural combinatorial interpretation in terms of centered primitive collections. We establish a general obstruction to being 2-Fano in terms of the existence of projective bundle structures and prove a birational reduction theorem for toric Fano manifolds with \(m(X)=2\). This allows us to show that the only toric 2-Fano manifold \(X\) with \(m(X) = 2\) is \(X\cong \mathbb{P}^2\). We also investigate how this strategy might extend to \(m\ge3\).
item.dc:creator: Carolina Araujo, Roya Beheshti, Ana-Maria Castravet, Kelly Jabbusch, Svetlana Makarova, Enrica Mazzon, Nivedita Viswanathan

item.title: A Peterson program for general Schubert varieties and mirror symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2609.30242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We initiate a `Peterson program' that seeks to extend Dale Peterson's theory for the quantum cohomology of flag varieties to arbitrary Schubert varieties, and that incorporates a mirror-symmetric approach. In this first paper we introduce a generalisation of the (localised) Peterson variety associated to an arbitrary Schubert variety $\check X_{w,P}$ inside a partial flag variety $\check G/\check P$. This generalisation is possibly a non-reduced affine scheme that lies in the Langlands dual full flag variety $G/B$. Additionally, we construct a Lie-theoretic `superpotential' associated to $\check X_{w,P}$, generalising earlier ones for the flag varieties $\check G/\check P$ from [Rie08], and we show that its relative critical point locus recovers the generalised Peterson variety. We make the key conjecture that for smooth Fano Schubert varieties the coordinate ring of the generalised Peterson variety recovers the quantum cohomology ring of $\check X_{w,P}$ localised at the quantum parameters. For smooth Fano Schubert varieties $X_{w,B}$ in $\check G/\check B$ we furthermore map our generalised Peterson variety to the cotangent bundle $\mathcal T^*(T)$ of the maximal torus $T$ of $G$ and construct a partial compactification that we conjecture models the full quantum cohomology ring of $\check X_{w,B}$, in analogy with the Givental-Kim presentation of $QH^*(\check G/\check B)$ via the degenerate leaf of the Kostant Toda lattice of $\check G$. These conjectures are verified for all smooth Schubert divisors in the complete type $A$ flag variety, and we show that our superpotential agrees with that introduced for Grassmannian Schubert varieties by Rietsch and Williams, after a suitable isomorphism of the domains.
item.dc:creator: Changzheng Li, Konstanze Rietsch, Mingzhi Yang

item.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16760v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the structure of \'etale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over rings of integers of number fields. We show that the image of the geometric \'etale fundamental group is FAb, while the kernel of the map to the fundamental group of the base need not be FAb or finitely generated. Our results rely on finiteness theorems for Galois coinvariants of geometric \'etale fundamental groups and \'etale cohomology over finitely generated fields. These apply to Galois extensions $L/k$ for which $\mathrm{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As a further application, we establish finiteness of prime-to-characteristic $L$-rational torsion on abelian varieties over $k$.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Steklov

item.title: The geometric exceptional set for Fano threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23024v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the geometric exceptional set in Manin's conjecture for smooth Fano threefolds. We prove that every adjoint rigid surface with $a$-invariant one on a non-product smooth Fano threefold is normal. This yields a description of the geometric exceptional set in terms of the higher-$a$ locus, anticanonical conics, and del Pezzo fibrations. Zariski density arises only from the latter two contributions. For del Pezzo fibrations, we construct a finite collection of parameter covers which control the associated breaking maps. We classify their low-genus components for general smooth Fano threefolds, yielding examples with potentially Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets in $22$ of the $105$ deformation families. Extending the construction of Batyrev and Tschinkel, we give examples of Fano fourfolds with quartic del Pezzo fibrations and an explicit Fano threefold with two del Pezzo fibrations of degree six. All these varieties have Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets. For the threefold, the original form of Manin's conjecture fails on every nonempty open subset for every anticanonical height.
item.dc:creator: Runxuan Gao

item.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33971v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.
item.dc:creator: Young-Hoon Kiem

item.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14283v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--P\u{a}un, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact K\"ahler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.
item.dc:creator: Tianshu Jiang, Jiayu Li

item.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
item.description: arXiv:2611.24361v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.
item.dc:creator: Fanjun Meng, Mihnea Popa

item.title: Incidence Correspondences and Chow Motives in the Symplectic (Z/2Z)4-K3 Locus
item.description: arXiv:2611.27800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a Chow-motivic framework for projective K3 surfaces with a symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action. For the universal Heisenberg-invariant quartic family, we show that the generically defined codimension-two cycles on the relative square are generated by three ambient classes and sixteen automorphism graphs, and that these nineteen classes are cohomologically independent. Combining this square-Franchetta property with a finite-cover trace construction and the Kuga-Satake correspondence, we prove that every smooth Heisenberg-invariant quartic K3 surface has a Chow motive of abelian type. We also consider the diagonal complete-intersection family of three quadrics and establish stability of the Heisenberg result under rational Hodge isogenies. For arbitrary projective K3 surfaces with a faithful symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action, we obtain a motivic reduction to the minimal resolution of the fifteen-node quotient. Applying a rational Kuga-Satake criterion, we establish abelianity of Chow motives for explicit infinite arithmetic subfamilies of all three Garbagnati-Sarti lattice types, including their Picard-rank specializations. Finally, we prove a square-Franchetta theorem for the ten-dimensional family of double-cubic K3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Sixuan Gu

item.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29033v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$
item.dc:creator: Raisa V. Serova, Anastasia V. Vikulova

item.title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
item.description: arXiv:2611.32354v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let $(X,B)$ be a projective log canonical pair with $X$ of Fano type, $-(K_X+B)$ nef and coefficients of $B$ in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all $\epsilon$-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of $\epsilon$. We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral $\Q$-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.
item.dc:creator: Xintong Jiang

item.title: Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II
item.description: arXiv:2308.00903v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we prove several transfer principles for the cohomological dimension of fields. Given a fixed field $K$ with finite cohomological dimension $\delta$, the two main ones allow to: - construct totally ramified extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq \delta - 1$ when $K$ is a complete discrete valuation field; - construct algebraic extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq \delta-1$ and satisfying a norm condition. We then apply these results to Serre's conjecture II and to some variants for fields of any cohomological dimension that are inspired by conjectures of Kato and Kuzumaki. In particular, we prove that Serre's conjecture II for characteristic $0$ fields implies Serre's conjecture II for positive characteristic fields.
item.dc:creator: Diego Izquierdo, Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche

item.title: Likelihood Geometry of Reflexive Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2311.13572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the problem of maximum likelihood (ML) estimation for statistical models defined by reflexive polytopes. Our focus is on the maximum likelihood degree of these models as an algebraic measure of complexity of the corresponding optimization problem. We compute the ML degrees of all 4319 classes of three-dimensional reflexive polytopes, and observe some surprising behavior in terms of the presence of gaps between ML degrees and degrees of the associated toric varieties. We interpret these drops in the context of discriminants and prove formulas for the ML degree for families of reflexive polytopes, including the hypercube and its dual, the cross polytope, in arbitrary dimension. In particular, we determine a family of embeddings for the $d$-cube that implies ML degree one. Finally, we discuss generalized constructions of families of reflexive polytopes in terms of their ML degrees.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Am\'endola, Janike Oldekop

item.title: On the Hermitian K-theory of Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2504.03969v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the $\mathbb{G}W$-spectrum (Karoubi--Grothendieck--Witt spectrum) of Grassmannians over divisorial schemes defined over fields of characteristic zero, and, as a corollary, determine their stabilized $\mathbb{L}$-theory spectrum. As part of our computation, we establish split fibration sequences in $\mathbb{K}$-theory, $\mathbb{G}W$-theory and $\mathbb{L}$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Sunny Sood, Chunkai Xu

item.title: The $d$-gonal locus in the moduli space of tropical plane curves
item.description: arXiv:2511.20805v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce and study the locus $\mathbb{M}_{g,d}^\textrm{nd}$ of genus $g$ tropical plane curves of gonality $d$ inside the moduli space $\mathbb{M}^{\textrm{nd}}_{g}$ of tropical plane curves of genus $g$. Each such tropical curve arises from a Newton polygon, and we conjecture that the gonality of the tropical curve is equal to an easily computed parameter of this polygon called the expected gonality, closely related to the lattice width of the polygon. Let $\mathbb{M}_{g,{\underline{d}}}^\textrm{nd}$ denote the locus of tropical curves whose associated Newton polygon has expected gonality $d$. We prove that for fixed $d$ and sufficiently large genus $g$, the dimensions of these two loci agree: \[ \\dim\left(\mathbb{M}_{g,d}^\textrm{nd}\right) =\dim\left(\mathbb{M}_{g,{\underline{d}}}^\textrm{nd}\right). \] Our results provide evidence that, in sufficiently high genus compared to expected gonality, the gonality of a tropical curve is determined by the expected gonality of the Newton polygon from which it arises. We also leverage our results to prove bounds on the dimensions of moduli spaces of non-degenerate algebraic curves.
item.dc:creator: Desmond Leitz, Ralph Morrison, S{\o}ren Newman-Taylor, Vincent X. Wang

item.title: On $F$-thresholds of differential power filtrations
item.description: arXiv:2607.09028v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the $F$-threshold of differential power filtrations of monomial ideals. We give the existence of this number and show that it is upper bounded by the maximum height of the minimal primes of the underlying monomial ideal. As an application of our results, we show that the dimension of the polynomial ring and the $F$-threshold of the differential power filtration of the monomial maximal ideal are the same.
item.dc:creator: W\'agner Badilla-C\'espedes

item.title: The arithmetic of critical values II: critical elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2608.29836v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this second chapter of the \textit{Arithmetic of critical values} series (ACV), we study certain double covers $E_f\to\mathbb{P}^1$ whose branch locus coincides with that of a quartic polynomial $f$. We give a direct proof of the fact, already shown non-constructively in ACV I, that the elliptic curves $E_f$ admit a $3$-isogeny. Our methods lead us to examine the Galois closure of $f:\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$, whose rich geometry yields a congruence between $E_f$ and a second elliptic curve $E'_f$. We study their arithmetic and show that they are linked by a Selmer companionship for infinitely many $f\in\mathbb{Z}[X]$, allowing us to exhibit elements in certain Tate-Shafarevich groups which are visible in an abelian surface. We also give some dynamical and Diophantine applications of our constructions, as well as new examples of Jacobians isogenous to a power of an elliptic curve.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Naccarato

item.title: A Note on Binary Quadratic Systems and their relation to complexity theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.07769v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deciding whether a system of multivariate quadratic equations over $\mathbb F_2$ has a solution is a classical NP-complete problem, and remains so for square systems, with as many equations as variables. The hardness of this problem is one of the cornerstones of nowadays post-quantum cryptography. Let $\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ and $\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ denote the sets of square quadratic systems in $n$ variables having respectively no solutions and exactly one solution. $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ is a coNP-complete language, while $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ lies in DP. It is known that $\lim_{n\to \infty} |\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)|/|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|=1$. Here we prove the explicit finite-$n$ bounds \[ |\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|<|\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)| \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|, \] More generally, let $Q_d$ be the space of polynomial functions $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n\to\mathbb F_2$ of degree at most $d$, and let $\alpha_k$ count square systems in $(Q_d)^n$ having exactly $k$ solutions. Then \[ \alpha_0<\alpha_1 \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)\alpha_0\,, \qquad 2\le d\le n \,. \] The proof combines matroid and coding-theoretic methods. We interpret $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ as the ground set of the evaluation matroid of $Q_d$, express $\alpha_0$ and $\alpha_1$ through characteristic polynomials, and use a Whitney-type sign-reversing involution to show that the only terms that can push $\alpha_1-\alpha_0$ below $\alpha_1/2^n$ come from the elements of a matroid port. These are identified with minimal-support words of the Reed--Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(n-d-1,n)=\mathrm{RM}(d,n)^\perp$; the required estimate then follows from the MacWilliams identity, the minimum-distance bound $2^{d+1}$, and the even-weight structure of the code.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Radici, Massimiliano Sala

item.title: Descartes' rule of signs for polynomial systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.06435v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The classical Descartes' rule of signs bounds the number of positive roots of a real polynomial in one variable by the number of sign changes of its coefficients. This bound only depends on the order of the exponents and on the signs of the coefficients, that is, on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices. We generalize this rule to fewnomial systems with any number of monomials: for systems of $n$ real polynomial equations in $n$ variables with $n+k+1$ monomials, we obtain upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate positive solutions which only depend on sign conditions on the maximal minors of the coefficient matrix and of the exponent matrix and its liftings. For $k=1$ they are the Descartes' rules of signs for circuits of Bihan--Dickenstein and Bihan--Dickenstein--Forsg{\aa}rd. Our approach starts from the Gale duality and the Khovanskii--Rolle argument of Bihan and Sottile, which reduce the problem to counting common zeros of iterated Jacobians in a chamber $\Delta$ of a hyperplane arrangement determined by the coefficients. We bound this number by the B\'ezout number minus the zeros forced in the other chambers by a topological degree, which we compute by a facet-count formula involving signs of minors of a Gale dual matrix of the exponent matrix. This leads to a recursion over the flats of the arrangement, which ends with the Descartes' rules for circuits. Restricting the recursion to coherent chambers, in which no cancellation occurs in the facet-count formula, gives weaker bounds in closed form.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: Topological degree of sparse polynomial maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.29808v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\A$, and we study the topological degree of $F$. We prove a real analogue of the Bernstein--Kushnirenko--Khovanskii theorem, which says that the number of solutions in the complex torus is the normalized volume of the Newton polytope when there is no solution at infinity. Our main assumption is a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope. It is a positive analogue of the absence of solutions at infinity, and it is satisfied for generic exponents and coefficients. Under this condition, we show that the topological degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We give two closed formulas for it: a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and a Viro formula, which is a signed count of the positively decorated simplices of a regular triangulation of $\A$. As a consequence, we get sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity results for their number.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: Integral permutation twisted cohomology: one auspicious twist is all you need
item.description: arXiv:2610.40602v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a reduced form of permutation twisted cohomology for the derived category of permutation modules over any commutative ring. Unlike the twisted cohomology rings previously constructed by Balmer--Gallauer and Miller, this reduced twisted cohomology ring is only bigraded, twisted by a single, well-chosen endotrivial complex corresponding to the representation sphere arising from the (doubled) regular real representation of a group. We prove that over any commutative ring, the Balmer spectrum of the derived category of permutation modules is homeomorphic to the projectivization of the spectrum of the reduced twisted cohomology ring. Moreover, we show that if the base ring is Noetherian, this ring is finite over the finitely generated subalgebra generated by the forerunners, certain $p$-local isomorphisms, of the twist. We apply these results to further analyze the geometry of permutation modules, determine the local Picard group of the geometric open of the Balmer spectrum, and resolve other questions posed by Miller. We include an appendix giving a general criterion for finite generation of twisted cohomology rings in tensor-triangular geometry.
item.dc:creator: Juan Omar G\'omez, Sam K. Miller

item.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.28178v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous \'etale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, where $\Omega_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Yunhao Sun

item.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.30682v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $\zeta_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: SeungJu Lee
